chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The sick person, if he cannot pray sitting, prays as he is able: either he turns [his body] and indicates with gestures. And he said: 'He turns as a man turns in his grave, and sleeps on his right side, then indicates with the prayer. If he cannot sleep on his right side, then as he is able is permissible for him, and he faces the Qiblah with his face, then indicates with the prayer with gestures.'
ai.seo_question: How should a sick person pray if they cannot sit or stand?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the flexibility in prayer postures for the severely ill, emphasizing that the obligation remains even when physical capacity is diminished. It specifically instructs that if one cannot sit, they should lie on their right side facing the Qiblah, mirroring the position of burial, and use eye or body gestures (*i'ma'*) for bowing and prostration. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of *takhyir* (ease) in worship, ensuring that the sick are not burdened beyond their physical limits while maintaining the integrity of the prayer ritual.
